drill_name: Youth Receiving Foundations — Quiet Glove & Soft Hands
description: First receiving progression for young catchers: glove presentation, soft hands, and catching the ball with slight momentum toward the strike zone. Fixes stabbing and hard hands behind the plate.
safety_notes: Use tennis balls or soft training balls for bare-hand/receiving-only work; full gear whenever catching live throws.
ai_coaching_notes: Start bare-glove with tennis balls from short distance. Cue 'catch the ball moving toward the zone, not away.' Watch for the elbow locking out — a slightly bent elbow keeps hands soft.
success_markers: Glove is quiet after the catch instead of drifting
Catches low pitches without turning the glove over
Ball stops moving toward the zone edge, not out of it

description: Five MLB-style receiving drills scalable to any age: beating the ball to the spot, sticking pitches, and working the edges of the zone. The middle step once basic soft hands are in place.
mechanic_focus: beat the ball to the spot
common_flaws_fixed: carrying pitches out of the zone
ai_coaching_notes: Run as a 5-station circuit. Cue 'beat it to the spot' — glove arrives where the pitch will be before the ball does. Freeze each catch for a one-count to build the stick habit.
success_markers: Borderline pitches are caught and held in the zone
Glove beats the ball to the spot on edges
Umpire-view video shows the ball 'stuck' rather than dragged

description: Modern one-knee-down receiving: five drills to master framing from the stance MLB catchers use, at higher pitch speeds. For experienced catchers ready for the progression ceiling.
common_flaws_fixed: carrying pitches out of the zone
ai_coaching_notes: Only introduce after two-knee receiving is consistent. Check the free leg still allows a block or throw. Increase pitch speed gradually — machine work is ideal for high-rep edges.
reps_guidance: 4 sets of 10 receives per setup (RH low, LH low, edges)
success_markers: Low strike is presented without dropping the glove head
Can still block and throw from one knee
Holds the bottom-zone strike at game velocity

drill_name: Blocking the Right Way — Technique to Reaction Reps
description: Correct blocking technique — knees replace the feet, chin tucks, chest angles the ball back toward the plate — built from stationary blocks into reaction reps to either side.
common_flaws_fixed: balls in the dirt get past
safety_notes: Full catcher's gear required for every blocking rep. Use soft training balls when learning; progress to baseballs only once form is consistent.
ai_coaching_notes: Start with placed balls (no throw) to groove the shape, then rolled balls, then short-hop throws. Cue 'round your shoulders, chin down, deaden it in front.' Left/right blocks push off the opposite foot.
success_markers: Ball dies within a 6-foot circle in front of the plate
Chin stays tucked — no flinch
Body beats the ball to the spot on lateral blocks

description: A game-speed blocking drill with unpredictable balls in the dirt — the catcher must read and react rather than pre-set. For catchers who already own solid blocking mechanics.
common_flaws_fixed: balls in the dirt get past
bails on balls in the dirt
safety_notes: Full catcher's gear required. Game-speed dirt balls only for catchers with established blocking form.
ai_coaching_notes: Mix locations randomly and don't telegraph. Score each rep: blocked-in-front = 2, blocked-away = 1, past = 0; track weekly. Add a runner-on-third scenario so recovery-to-throw matters.
success_markers: 8+ of 10 random balls kept in front
Recovers to throwing position within one second
No flinch or head-turn at game velocity

description: Catcher footwork patterns for throwing to second at game speed — replace, jab-step, and transfer mechanics that shorten pop time and control the running game.
safety_notes: Arm-care warm-up before throw-downs; cap volume at ~20 full-intensity throws per session for youth arms.
ai_coaching_notes: Time every rep glove-to-glove. Cue 'feet start the throw' — the exchange happens while the feet replace. Start dry (no ball), then from a partner's toss, then live machine pitches.
success_markers: Pop time trends down week over week
Transfer happens during footwork, not after
Throws arrive on the bag-side of second consistently

drill_name: Bent-Leg Slide Basics — The Right Way to Slide
description: Intro to correct bent-leg sliding: when to start the slide, tucking one leg into the figure-4, keeping hands up, and avoiding the habits that cause injuries.
safety_notes: No headfirst slides for beginners. Slide on grass, wet grass, or a mat before ever sliding on dirt; remove cleats for first sessions.
ai_coaching_notes: Teach on grass in socks or on a sliding mat first — never on dirt day one. Cue 'sit into it, hands to the sky.' Start from a walk, then jog, then run. Mark a start line about two body lengths from the base.
reps_guidance: 10-15 slides per session, building speed gradually
success_markers: Slides on the seat/hip, not the knees
Hands stay up through the slide
Starts the slide at the marked distance without hesitation

description: Station-based sliding reps for teams: high-repetition bent-leg slides in a controlled setting to build comfort and consistency once players know the basic form.
safety_notes: Use mats or grass for volume work; check the sliding lane is clear of equipment between reps.
ai_coaching_notes: Run as a rotating station during practice. Every player gets volume without dirt burn. Watch for the trail leg flattening out — keep the figure-4. Add a coach pointing left/right so runners slide to a side of the bag.
success_markers: Same slide shape every rep
Can slide to either side of the bag on command
No slowing down before the slide starts

description: Game-speed pop-up slide: sliding into the bag on the bent leg and using momentum to pop up ready to advance on an overthrow.
safety_notes: Full-speed pop-up slides on dirt only after mat/grass mastery; no headfirst variations.
ai_coaching_notes: Only after the basic bent-leg slide is automatic. Cue 'slide through the bag, not to it' — momentum carries the runner up onto the planted foot. Pair with a coach throwing simulated overthrows to train the advance read.
reps_guidance: 8-10 pop-up slides, last 4 with an overthrow read
success_markers: Pops to standing without using hands
Eyes find the ball immediately after the slide
Advances confidently on overthrows in scrimmages

drill_name: Steal Breaks — Reading the Pitcher & First Move
description: Teaches the steal break: what runners watch on the pitcher, when to take off, and the explosive crossover first move. Coach-facing so it translates straight to team practice.
ai_coaching_notes: Line the whole team up off an imaginary first base facing a coach simulating a pitcher. On first move: break. Cue 'sink, cross over, run through second's back corner.' Call out what tipped the pitcher's move each rep.
reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 6 breaks (react to leg lift, first move, pickoff mix)
success_markers: Breaks on first move, not on a guess
Crossover step gains ground toward second
Freezes correctly on pickoff moves

description: The secondary lead and the delayed steal: timing shuffles with the pitch, reading the catcher, and stealing bases without elite speed.
ai_coaching_notes: Rep the two-shuffle secondary timed to the pitch crossing the zone. For the delayed steal, break as the catcher's throw goes back to the pitcher. Works especially well at levels where catchers lob returns.
success_markers: Secondary lead lands as the pitch crosses the plate
Momentum moving toward the next base at contact
Successfully times a delayed steal in scrimmage

drill_name: Pro Base-Stealing Package — Leads, Reads & Jumps
description: Game-speed stealing package: primary lead distance, reading pitcher tells and pickoff moves, and maximizing the jump against live pitching.
equipment_needed: live pitcher or coach on mound
ai_coaching_notes: Run against a live pitcher working from the stretch. Chart every rep: safe jump / late / picked. Teach one tell at a time (heel lift, shoulder lean, head pattern). Time first-move-to-second and track improvement.
success_markers: Identifies the pitcher's tell and states it out loud
Jump rate improves on the weekly chart
Returns standing on pickoffs — never dives late from an overextended lead

description: A simplified cut-and-relay system built for Little League fields: where each fielder goes on balls to each outfield spot, kept simple enough for young teams to run in games.
safety_notes: Sequence throws so only one ball is live at a time; young fielders should never turn their back on an incoming throw.
ai_coaching_notes: Walk the whole team through each scenario at half speed with no ball first — every player physically moves to their spot. Then add a rolled ball, then a thrown ball. Quiz players: 'ball in the right-center gap, runner on first — where do you go?'
reps_guidance: Walk-through of 4 scenarios, then 2 live reps each
success_markers: Every player moves somewhere on contact — nobody stands still
Cutoff man is in line between outfielder and target base
Team can name their assignment for each gap without prompting

drill_name: Line Relay Race — Catch, Turn, Throw
description: A repeatable line-relay drill: lining up to the ball, presenting a big target with hands up, and making quick catch-turn-throw transfers down the line. Run it as a race between two lines.
safety_notes: Match throwing distances to arm strength — shorten the links for 8-10U rather than letting kids max-effort long throws.
ai_coaching_notes: Two lines of 4-5 players, 60-90 feet apart per link. Cue 'big hands, catch, turn glove-side, throw through the chest.' First line to run the ball down and back wins. Shrink spacing for younger kids.
success_markers: Relay man's hands are up calling for the ball before it arrives
Turns glove-side automatically
Ball travels line-to-line without hitting the ground

description: Team cutoff and relay responsibilities by situation — who the cutoff man is on balls to each outfield spot, and how infielders and outfielders communicate to hit the cutoff.
safety_notes: One live ball at a time; runners wear helmets during live cutoff reps.
ai_coaching_notes: Add runners so decisions are real: runner on first, ball to left-center — where's the throw? Let the cutoff man call 'cut two / cut three / let it go' loudly. Rotate players through cutoff roles so everyone learns both ends.
success_markers: Outfield throws come down through the cutoff man's head height
Cutoff man makes a loud call on every ball
Correct base chosen on 4 of 5 situational reps

drill_name: Machine-Fed Relay Sequences at Game Speed
description: Game-speed cutoff and relay team sequences modeled on Vanderbilt's practice, using machine-fed balls to rep full outfield-to-infield relays at high tempo.
safety_notes: Full-intensity relay throws count toward daily throwing volume — run this early in practice on fresh arms.
ai_coaching_notes: Machine or fungo fires balls into the gaps on a fixed interval so tempo never drops. Run double-cut sequences on balls to the wall. Score runs-prevented vs. bases-gained to make it competitive between defensive groups.
reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 5 relay sequences at full speed
success_markers: Relay throws are caught chest-high moving toward the target
Double cut executes with the trail man communicating
Sequence time from outfield touch to tag drops week over week

description: A simple pickle setup — two bases, two fielders, one runner — teaching kids to run hard at the runner, hold the ball up, and make one crisp throw for the tag.
safety_notes: Runners wear helmets; tags applied with the glove, no arm swings at head height.
ai_coaching_notes: Cue 'run him back, ball up by your ear, one throw.' The receiving fielder calls 'now!' for the throw. Rotate every player through both fielder spots and runner. Count throws out loud — celebrate one-throw outs.
success_markers: Fielder sprints at the runner instead of hesitating
Ball stays visible above the shoulder — no pump fakes
Most outs recorded in two throws or fewer

drill_name: Calm Rundowns — Push Back, Follow Your Throw
description: Takes the panic out of youth rundowns: pushing the runner back toward the previous base, following your throw, and getting the out in as few throws as possible.
safety_notes: Helmets on runners; keep rundown lanes clear of bats and loose balls.
ai_coaching_notes: Layer in the rule: always push the runner back toward the base he came from, and always follow your throw to the end of the opposite line. Add a second runner variant once the basic rotation is automatic.
success_markers: Runner is always moving back toward the trailing base
Thrower follows his throw every time without reminding
Backup fielder is in line before the throw is made

description: Pro-level rundown execution at game speed — sprinting to close distance, ball visible above the shoulder, dart-throw timing, and rotating behind the play.
safety_notes: Game-speed dart throws at short range demand focus — receivers give a clear target away from the runner's head, and runners wear helmets.
ai_coaching_notes: Use your fastest players as runners and score it: out in ≤2 throws = defense wins. Cue 'sprint, show, dart' — full-speed close, ball shown early, short dart throw on the receiver's call. Rotate at full speed.
success_markers: Defense wins 80% of reps vs. fast runners
Dart throws released on the receiver's call — never early
Rotation continues seamlessly through multiple throws when needed

drill_name: First Base Fundamentals — Finding the Bag & the Stretch
description: Core first-base play: getting to the bag, setting the feet, and basic stretch mechanics to receive throws. The starting point before picks and off-line throws.
ai_coaching_notes: Cue 'find it with your feet, face the thrower, stretch on release — not before.' Rep the footwork with no ball first: sprint to the bag from fielding depth, find it, set. Then add easy chest-high throws.
reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 8 reps (footwork only, then with throws)
success_markers: Finds the bag without looking down
Stretch happens as the throw is released, not as the fielder arrives
Heel contact maintained through the catch

description: Youth-specific work around the bag from a former pro: adjusting the feet to the throw and stretching to balls at different locations, with repeatable practice drills.
ai_coaching_notes: Throw intentionally to all four quadrants. Cue 'chase the ball with your glove-side foot' — the stretch foot moves toward the throw while the anchor toe holds the bag edge. Mix in throws from different infield angles.
reps_guidance: 4 rounds of 6 throws (one round per quadrant)
success_markers: Stretch foot mirrors the throw location automatically
Anchor foot stays on the bag on wide throws
Clean catches on throws to both sides without crossing feet

drill_name: Advanced First Base — Off-Line Throws, Picks & Short Hops
description: Academy-level footwork around the bag: shifting for throws to either side, timing the stretch, and picking short hops — the stretch goal for travel-level first basemen.
safety_notes: Short-hop volume is hard on the glove hand — use tennis balls or soft baseballs for high-rep sessions.
ai_coaching_notes: Feed short hops on purpose — start with announced hops, progress to random. Cue 'soft glove through the hop, not at it.' Add baserunner pressure last: a runner sprinting the line forces real stretch timing.
reps_guidance: 3 sets of 8 picks (announced, random, with runner)
success_markers: Picks 6+ of 8 random short hops cleanly
Chooses stretch vs. leave-the-bag correctly on wild throws
Footwork holds up with a live runner

description: Five daily backhand drills training glove angle, footwork, and body position on balls to the glove-side and backhand side — the range and glove control travel-ball infielders need.
ai_coaching_notes: Run as a daily 10-minute series from knees to full speed. Cue 'thumb down, see the ball into the glove, work through it.' The right foot plants outside the ball on a true backhand — check plant position every rep.
success_markers: Fields backhands with the glove out front — not beside the body
Plant foot consistently outside the ball
Converts backhand to throw without extra steps

description: Rapid-fire three-ball slow roller drill: charge, field on the run, and throw on the move under time pressure — the do-or-die play against fast runners.
safety_notes: Throwing on the run stresses the arm — full warm-up first and cap circuits for youth arms.
ai_coaching_notes: Three balls spaced progressively closer — the fielder charges, fields, and throws each in sequence with no reset. Cue 'right foot, left foot, throw' rhythm on the run. Bare-hand only when the ball has stopped.
success_markers: Fields the ball outside the glove-side foot on the run
Throw releases within two steps of fielding
Accurate to first on all three balls of a circuit

description: Double-play footwork, feeds, and pivots at second base for both middle-infield positions — game-speed exchange and turn mechanics for 12-14U middle infielders.
common_flaws_fixed: slow transitions from catch to throw
safety_notes: Teach bag footwork that clears the runner's path; no live hard slides in practice turns.
ai_coaching_notes: Rep feeds first (chest-high, at the bag), then turns without a runner, then with a soft slide. Cue 'give him the ball where his hands start.' Alternate 4-6-3 and 6-4-3 every round so both players learn both ends.
success_markers: Feeds arrive chest-high at the bag every rep
Pivot man's exchange takes one step or fewer
Full turn (contact to first-base catch) under a coach-set time target

drill_name: Call It Early — Outfield Communication Basics
description: Introduces calling the ball — loud, early 'mine, mine, mine' between outfielders — with a simple drill format that builds the habit and prevents collisions.
ai_coaching_notes: Toss high flies between two fielders. Rule: the call must come before the ball's peak, three times loud. The other player answers 'take it, take it' and peels away. Start with soft balls so nobody fears the collision.
success_markers: Call comes before the ball peaks
Non-catching player audibly yields and peels off
Zero silent drops between fielders in scrimmages

description: A practice-plan drill covering fly-ball priority between infielders and outfielders — who calls it, who peels off — plus ready-position habits, straight from the ABCA.
ai_coaching_notes: Hit tweeners between the infield and outfield on purpose. Teach the rule plainly: the outfielder coming in owns any ball he can reach — infielders yield to his call. Freeze the play after each rep and ask 'whose ball, and why?'
success_markers: Outfielder's call overrides the infielder every time
Infielder peels off without stopping in the landing zone
Tweeners get caught instead of dropping between frozen fielders

description: The outfield do-or-die play: charging a ground ball hard, fielding off the glove-side foot, and releasing quickly to cut down a runner at the plate.
safety_notes: Max-effort throws — warm up fully and cap at 8 reps per session for youth arms.
ai_coaching_notes: Only for game-on-the-line situations — teach the distinction from the routine knee-down block. Cue 'attack, glove-side foot, crow hop through the ball.' Chart throw time and accuracy to a plate-sized target.
success_markers: Fielding happens off the glove-side foot at speed
Momentum continues through the throw toward the target
Throw is catchable at the plate on a line or one long hop

description: Step-by-step introduction to holding and throwing a traditional changeup, built for youth hands: burying the ball deep in the palm and throwing with fastball intent.
safety_notes: The changeup is the safe first off-speed pitch for youth arms — no curveball spin. Keep total throwing volume within normal daily limits.
ai_coaching_notes: Start at short distance playing catch with the grip — no mound. Cue 'throw the fastball, the grip does the work.' If the ball sails, the grip is too shallow; if it dies into the dirt, too deep. Find the middle.
reps_guidance: 15-20 changeup throws within a normal catch session
success_markers: Arm speed looks identical to the fastball from behind
Ball comes out 8-10% slower without being aimed
Comfortable enough to throw it in a bullpen without hesitation

drill_name: Teaching the Changeup — Fastball Arm, Slower Ball
description: A pro coach's method for developing the changeup with young pitchers: grip selection for small hands and keeping arm speed identical to the fastball so the pitch actually deceives.
safety_notes: Introduce off-speed only after fastball mechanics are stable; changeup before any breaking ball for youth pitchers.
ai_coaching_notes: Film from the side: the fastball and changeup deliveries should be indistinguishable. Common fault is slowing the arm — fix it by cueing 'throw it hard' and letting the grip kill velocity. Mix 1 changeup per 3 fastballs in bullpens.
reps_guidance: 10-12 changeups per bullpen, mixed with fastballs
success_markers: Side-by-side video shows matching arm speed
Changeup lands in the bottom half of the zone
Hitters in live BP are visibly out in front

drill_name: Changeup Grip Menu — Match the Grip to the Hand
description: Walks through circle, three-finger, and other changeup grip options so pitchers can match a grip to their hand size as they grow — and refine feel and movement.
safety_notes: Grip experiments stay within normal catch-play volume; no max-effort mound work while testing grips.
ai_coaching_notes: Have the pitcher test 2-3 grips over two weeks of catch play and keep whichever kills the most speed with the least effort. Small hands usually can't do a true circle — three-finger is the honest starting point. Revisit each off-season as hands grow.
reps_guidance: 10 throws per grip during catch play
frequency_guidance: 2-3x/week for two weeks, then settle on one
success_markers: Picks one grip and can describe why it fits
Consistent 8-12% speed gap off the fastball
Some arm-side fade develops as pronation improves

drill_name: The Catch Drill — Track & Read Pitches
description: Hitters catch pitches instead of swinging, training the eyes to read pitch type and location out of the hand — recognition and discipline without swing pressure.
safety_notes: Helmet required when standing in the box; start with reduced-speed pitching for younger hitters.
ai_coaching_notes: Hitter stands in the box wearing a helmet with a glove and catches the pitch, calling 'fastball' or 'change' as early as possible. Score correct early calls. Rotate hitters standing in during bullpens for free reps.
success_markers: Calls pitch type before the ball is halfway home
Correctly takes balls and 'catches strikes' by location call
Carries calmer takes into live at-bats

description: What 'staying back' actually means, with drills to keep weight and hands loaded so hitters aren't fooled out front by off-speed pitches.
ai_coaching_notes: Front toss with random speed changes: the feeder varies fast/slow without telling. Cue 'stride to hit the fastball, keep the hands back for the change.' The stride lands on time — the hands wait.
success_markers: Head and weight stay behind the front hip on slow pitches
Hard contact on both speeds within the same round
No double-stride or lunge when fooled

description: The correct in-swing adjustment when a hitter recognizes off-speed mid-pitch — keeping the barrel in the zone instead of rolling over, for hitters facing pitchers who mix speeds.
ai_coaching_notes: Machine or feeder mixes speeds with a 2:1 fastball bias. Cue 'swing fastball, adjust down and long' — the barrel stays through the hitting zone so late recognition still produces fair contact. Track hard-hit rate on the off-speed only.
success_markers: Off-speed contact goes up the middle or oppo instead of weak pull-side
Posture holds through the adjusted swing
Hard-hit rate on off-speed climbs over 3-4 sessions

description: Five coach-friendly methods for teaching hitters to drive the ball the other way — the foundation for hitting behind runners and executing situational at-bats.
ai_coaching_notes: Start on the tee set deep in the zone. Cue 'let it get to your back hip, hit the inside half.' Progress through the five methods as each sticks. Success is direction, not distance — a firm ground ball the other way counts.
reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 10 swings, all must go opposite field
success_markers: Ball flight consistently between center and the opposite-field line
Contact point is visibly deeper than the pull-side swing
Can call 'oppo' and execute on demand in BP

drill_name: Oppo Tee & Toss — Stay Inside the Ball
description: A repeatable tee/toss drill for staying inside the ball and driving outside pitches the other way — plugs directly into situational BP rounds.
ai_coaching_notes: Tee on the outer third, slightly deep. Cue 'knob to the ball, barrel late.' Rolling over the outside pitch means the barrel released early — reset with three one-arm bottom-hand swings, then return to full swings.
reps_guidance: 4 sets of 8 swings on the outer-third tee
success_markers: Line drives to the opposite gap off the outer-third tee
No rolled-over contact for a full set
Same swing shows up on outside pitches in front toss

description: The 'move 'em' at-bat — advancing a runner from second with nobody out — broken down with College World Series examples: approach, pitch zones, and execution under pressure.
ai_coaching_notes: Run situational BP: runner at second, nobody out, hitter must move him. Only pitches middle-away get swings — pulling a ball on the ground to short is a failed rep even if it's a 'hit.' Score execution, not outcomes.
reps_guidance: 2 situational rounds of 6 at-bat scenarios per session
success_markers: Runner reaches third on 4+ of 6 execution reps
Hitter can state the plan before stepping in
Takes the inside pitch he can't execute with, without frustration

description: Overload/underload training with weighted and light bats to raise bat speed in youth hitters — how to sequence heavy-light swings safely for developing players.
safety_notes: Keep overload bats within ~20% of game bat weight for youth; stop if wrist or elbow soreness appears.
ai_coaching_notes: Order matters: heavy (feel sequence) → light (move fast) → game bat (transfer). Full intent on every swing — lazy overload swings teach slow. Measure with a swing sensor or simple phone video if no sensor.
success_markers: Game-bat swing speed measurably up over 4-6 weeks
Swing sequence stays intact under the heavy bat
No grip/wrist soreness — load is age-appropriate

description: A simple high-rep bunting drill that trains deadening the ball and placing bunts toward first or third on command — precision beyond basic technique.
ai_coaching_notes: Lay towels or cone lanes down each line. Feeder calls 'first side' or 'third side' mid-toss. Cue 'catch it with the barrel' — soft top hand gives with contact. Chase the ball angle with the knob, not the barrel.
reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 10 bunts, alternating target lanes
success_markers: 7+ of 10 bunts stop inside the called lane
Ball dies within 15 feet of the plate
Bat starts at the top of the zone — anything above it is taken

description: A team-wide competitive bunting game scoring sacrifice bunts, push bunts, and bunting for a hit — pressure and accountability so bunting practice transfers to games.
ai_coaching_notes: Split the team; each hitter draws a situation card (sac to third, push past the pitcher, squeeze). Points only for executed bunts against live pitching. Losing team does field cleanup — pressure makes the reps real.
success_markers: Executes 3 different bunt types against live pitching
Success rate climbs across sessions
Players choose the right bunt for the situation without coaching

description: Essential J-band resistance exercises for youth pitchers and throwers: warming up the shoulder and building arm strength before any throwing session.
safety_notes: Light resistance only for youth — bands should bend, not strain. Stop any exercise that causes joint pain rather than muscle warmth.
ai_coaching_notes: Anchor at elbow height and keep tension light — these are activation reps, not strength maxes. Cue 'slow out, slow back' with no band snap. Make it the non-negotiable first station before any throwing.
reps_guidance: 1 round of 8-10 reps per exercise, before every throwing session
success_markers: Completes the routine without form breakdown
Reports the arm feeling 'ready' before the first throw
Routine happens without being reminded

description: A nine-exercise J-band routine targeting the rotator cuff and scapular muscles for throwing durability and velocity — proper band tension, tempo, and the common form mistakes.
safety_notes: Strength band work belongs on low-throwing days; skip it the day after a max pitch-count outing.
ai_coaching_notes: Run as a standalone mini-workout on lighter throwing days, not tacked onto a max-effort session. Cue controlled 2-second tempo each direction. Elbows stay at the set height — dropping the elbow is the giveaway fatigue sign to stop.
success_markers: All 9 exercises completed with steady tempo
Band resistance can progress after 3-4 weeks
Arm bounces back faster between outings

description: Eight exercises pitchers should do after bullpens or game outings to flush the arm and protect the rotator cuff — a consistent recovery habit between outings.
safety_notes: Recovery work is light by design — no heavy resistance after throwing. Persistent sharp pain after outings is a see-a-doctor sign, not a push-through sign.
ai_coaching_notes: The routine happens within 15 minutes of the last pitch, every outing — consistency is the entire point. Keep everything light and rhythmic; recovery work should feel easier than warm-up work. Log soreness the next day to show players it works.
reps_guidance: 1 round of 8 exercises immediately after throwing
frequency_guidance: After every bullpen, start, or heavy throwing day
success_markers: Next-day soreness noticeably reduced in the player's log
Routine completed unprompted after outings
Full pain-free range of motion maintained through the season
